_readme: Cross-language conformance fixture for the password policy.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the hub enforces the policy (backend/util/validate/password.go)
and the browser hand-mirrors it (frontend/src/lib/validate.ts validatePassword) so a
signup, setup, or profile form can refuse a bad password at the field instead of after
a round trip. A mirror that nobody checks stops matching. This file is that check:
both suites read it, so EDITING ONE SIDE WITHOUT THE OTHER IS THE EXACT BUG IT
PREVENTS -- the language that drifts is the one whose CI turns red.
The drift this fixture was written for was live: the hub measured the length with
Go's `len` (UTF-8 BYTES) and the browser measured it with `String.length` (UTF-16
CODE UNITS), and both messages said `characters`, which is neither count. A 43
character CJK password is 43 code units and 129 bytes, so the browser accepted it and
the hub then refused it as too long. The rule now accepts a printable ASCII character
only, which makes one character one byte and one code unit at the same time, so the
two limits are one rule. The case at repeat 43 is that exact password.
THE CHARACTER SET: 0x20 (the space) through 0x7E (the tilde) inclusive, and nothing
else. The space is allowed anywhere, at the start and at the end included, because
neither side trims a password -- a passphrase with spaces is a good password. The
control block 0x00-0x1F and DEL (0x7F) are refused: such a character reaches a
password field through a paste accident or a terminal control sequence, never through
deliberate typing. Every character above 0x7E is refused too, and that half of the
rule is what keeps one character equal to one byte.
CONSUMED BY (keep both in sync with this schema):
Go: backend/util/validate/password_test.go   TestValidatePasswordConformance
TS: frontend/src/lib/validate.test.ts        validatePassword conformance block
THE CONTRACT, per case: the password is `password` repeated `repeat` times (`repeat`
is optional and defaults to 1; it exists so a boundary reads as the NUMBER 128 rather
than as 128 characters a reader has to count). Both sides assert:
the validator accepts the password iff `valid`
a refused password reports the rule named by `refusal`
`refusal` is one of `too_short`, `too_long`, `not_printable_ascii`, and is empty when
`valid`. Each suite maps the token to a marker in its own message, because the two
messages differ by the leading capital only. Asserting the token is what pins the
ORDER of the rules: the character-set rule runs BEFORE both length rules on both
sides, so a password that is both too short and outside the character set reports
the character set and not the length.
WRITING A CASE: write every character outside 0x20-0x7E as a JSON escape, the way
each case below does. A raw control byte inside a JSON string is invalid JSON and
fails loudly, but a raw DEL (0x7F) byte is VALID JSON and invisible in an editor --
the case would then pin a rule nobody can read.
`why` is documentation only; neither suite asserts on it.

cases.why: empty
one below the minimum
the minimum length
a typical password
digits only: there is no complexity rule
the maximum length
one above the maximum
every ASCII punctuation mark is allowed
a passphrase: a space between two words is allowed
spaces only: 0x20 is the bottom of the printable range, and neither side trims a password
a leading space and a trailing space both survive: neither side trims a password
the tilde (0x7E) is the top of the printable range
NUL (0x00) is the bottom of the control block
a tab is ASCII but not printable
a newline: the character a pasted line carries
0x1F, one below the printable range
DEL (0x7F), one above the printable range
too short AND unprintable: the character-set rule reports first
too long AND unprintable: the character-set rule reports first
Latin-1 umlauts: accepted by both sides before the character-set rule
128 code units, 256 bytes: the browser accepted this and the hub refused it
43 CJK characters: 43 code units, 129 bytes -- the drift case that motivated the rule
too short AND outside the printable range: the character-set rule reports first
too long AND outside the printable range: the character-set rule reports first
an astral emoji: one character, 2 code units, 4 bytes
a lone surrogate: Go decodes it to U+FFFD and the browser keeps the code unit, and both are outside the printable range
